summary.name: Revu
summary.one_liner: Revu is an open-source, local-first flashcard and study app with FSRS spaced repetition, with a native macOS app (Revu Classic, free and GPL 3) and an AI-powered web version (Revu Web) in progress.
use_cases: Studying for exams with spaced repetition
Importing existing Anki decks into a macOS app
Offline flashcard review on a Mac
Turning lecture slides and PDFs into flashcards
Planning a weekly study schedule around calendar events
Sharing study materials within a small group
summary.what_it_does: Revu Classic is a native macOS study app that uses the FSRS algorithm to schedule flashcard reviews, supporting Q&A, cloze and multiple-choice cards, coverage mapping, and importing Anki decks, with local-first storage and full offline support. Revu Web, which is marked as coming soon, is described as adding AI generation of flashcards, practice exams and study guides from PDFs, slides and photos of notes, plus autopilot weekly planning, calendar sync with Google Calendar and Apple ICS, and session structures. The page also lists a free three-minute set of browser-based memory assessments (flash recall, term matching, digit span). Pricing for the web tiers is listed in euros, with a pod option that splits a paid seat among up to five people.
notable: Revu Classic is free and open source under GPL 3, with local-first storage and full offline support
Imports Anki decks and uses the FSRS scheduling algorithm
AI generation and calendar-aware autopilot scheduling are planned for Revu Web but marked coming soon
Study Pods let up to five people share materials with separate FSRS progress per person
caveats: Revu Web's AI features are listed as coming soon, with only a waitlist available
Revu Web Pro costs €19.99 per month, and the Plus plan is €9.99 per month
Revu Classic is macOS only per the page
